title: How biomedical foundation models turn literature and other biological data into training corpora
timestamp_policy: Human-facing generation time is fixed PST (UTC-8). The directory date is the UTC research date.
scope: 17 model families and three training-data studies, emphasizing scientific literature acquisition, post-extraction curation, continued pretraining, mixtures, structured biology, synthetic data, and training-value evidence. Medical generalists are identified separately from biological research models.
method: Targeted web searches, citation following, and reading primary papers, official technical reports, and author repositories. This is a broad targeted review, not an exhaustive systematic census or a common-protocol model leaderboard. Unknown details remain unknown.
execution: Literature review and small source snapshots only. No new OCR, model inference, training, paid teacher generation, GPU allocation, or bulk paper collection. Existing experiments and scores are unchanged.
interpretation_rules: Corpus tokens, training tokens consumed, distinct papers, abstracts, packed sequences, and image-caption pairs are different units. Counts across models overlap and must not be added.
PMC-derived does not establish whether a model used XML, PDFs, or an upstream extraction. A missing OCR description is not evidence that OCR was never used upstream.

Continued pretraining (CPT) means additional language-model training on a domain corpus. Instruction tuning (SFT) means training on task prompts and target responses. Older papers sometimes call both fine-tuning.
A teacher's educational-quality score is a curation signal, not scientific truth or independently adjudicated extraction ground truth.
Published benchmark numbers below are author-reported and protocol-specific. They are not measurements from our 50-paper extraction experiment.
Clinical evidence ranking and exclusion of animal studies should not be copied into a corpus intended for biological research.

models.name: BioGPT
models.corpus: 15M PubMed records with both title and abstract, updated before 2021.
models.document_route: Download PubMed records from the official FTP distribution; title-plus-abstract text, rather than full paper PDFs.
models.curation: Discard entries without an abstract. Learn an in-domain BPE vocabulary.
models.training_unit_and_mix: Biomedical autoregressive pretraining; downstream tasks use task-specific prompts and target formats.
models.augmentation: Full-paper OCR and a general replay mixture are not the reported core recipe.
models.evidence: Evaluates relation extraction, QA, document classification, and generation; these evaluate the trained model, not PDF extraction accuracy.
models.disclosure_gap: Fifteen million records must not be described as fifteen million full-text papers.

models.name: PMC-LLaMA
models.corpus: 4.8M PMC-ID-selected S2ORC papers, over 75B tokens; 30K textbooks yielding approximately 4B tokens.
models.document_route: Papers arrive through S2ORC. Textbook text is extracted from PDFs; a specific OCR engine is not identified in the reviewed method.
models.curation: Textbook deduplication and removal of URLs, author lists, contents, references, citations, and figure/table mentions.
models.training_unit_and_mix: Batch token ratio is BOOKS:PAPERS:GENERAL = 15:4:1; RedPajama supplies general replay.
models.augmentation: SFT adds GPT-4 instruction paraphrases, ChatGPT-generated QA explanations, and UMLS entity/relationship prompts; 202M instruction tokens.
models.evidence: Includes component ablations and medical QA evaluation.
models.disclosure_gap: The large paper corpus does not mean papers dominate the sampled training mixture. Early paper-only 7B versions differ from the later recipe.

data_records.source_section: Published models make different choices

fields.Reported treatment: Removes references and citations during textbook cleaning. The report does not establish that this same policy was applied to its entire paper corpus. [Dataset-I: Books](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.14454v3)

notes: PMC-LLaMA defines one epoch as seeing the book tokens once and trains for five such epochs. It does not mean five passes over its >75B paper pool. I have not replaced the reported schedule with a falsely precise consumed-token estimate. [PMC-LLaMA, Combination / Knowledge Injection Training](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.14454v3)

**PMC-LLaMA:** Samples textbook, paper and general-domain tokens at 15:4:1 for knowledge-injection CPT. Its UMLS prompts and generated QA explanations belong to the later instruction stage. [Dataset-I and Dataset-II](https://arxiv.org/html/2304.14454v3)

models.name: BioMistral
models.stage: CPT; evaluation with few-shot prompts and SFT
models.corpus: 3B-token sample of the commercial-use PMC-OA subset; approximately 1.47M reported documents, 98.75% English.
models.document_route: Raw article text from PMC-OA; the paper does not specify a reproducible PDF-versus-XML conversion engine.
models.curation: License-based selection, prioritizing non-English documents, then filling the token budget with English documents.
models.training_unit_and_mix: 1.5 epochs; EOS-delimited packing into 2,048-token sequences without padding. General capability retention is also explored through weight merging with the original model.
models.augmentation: No teacher-written expansion is required for its core PMC CPT stage.
models.evidence: Few-shot Table 2 averages: plain BioMistral 50.3 versus parent 51.2; SLERP-merged variant 55.4. Adaptation is not uniformly beneficial.
models.disclosure_gap: The reported document count is not independently verified as distinct complete papers.

models.name: MEDITRON
models.corpus: GAP-Replay: 48.1B tokens including validation; approximately 5M full texts, 16.1M abstracts, 46K guidelines, and 420M general replay tokens.
models.document_route: S2ORC text and annotations; upstream GROBID table extraction is explicitly discussed. Guidelines have a separate scraping/cleaning path.
models.curation: English/ID deduplication; remove author/bibliography sections. Keep figure/table captions, discard unreliable table bodies, expand citation and figure references with tagged short descriptions.
models.augmentation: Structured reference rewriting is not teacher-generated scientific reasoning.
models.evidence: 7B trial Table 8: PMC 54.6; PMC+Replay 56.2; clinically upsampled PMC 54.7; GAP+Replay 58.9 average accuracy.
models.disclosure_gap: Clinical upsampling is an ablation, not the final best recipe; filtering animal studies is inappropriate for a general biology corpus.

notes: BioMatrix's scientific text uses FineFineWeb biology/chemistry/medicine/health and literature; its figure also names bioRxiv. No numeric paper/web split is supplied. Figure 3 subdivides protein tokens into **36.0B sequence / 38.5B structure / 2.9B other**; molecule tokens into **32.1B sequence / 17.6B structure / 24.0B other**; cross-entity tokens into **17.1B sequence / 11.4B structure / 19.5B other**. The “other” subdivisions should not be relabeled entirely as generated text. Sources include PubChem, UniRef/UniProt, PDB/AFDB, interaction datasets and GPT-generated MolTextNet descriptions; exact individual budgets remain NR. These modalities are biomolecular representations, not paper-figure pixels. [BioMatrix, Figure 3 and §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.22138v1#page=12)

**BioMatrix:** Continues Qwen3 on 304.4B tokens spanning literature/web text, PubChem records, protein sequences and structures, interactions and interleaved text/entities. It includes GPT-generated MolTextNet descriptions and computational structures as well as experimental PDB structures. Its TrEMBL branch explicitly removes literature citations and evidence codes. These provenance differences should remain visible in a scientific corpus. [§3.1–3.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.22138v1)

recommended_experiments_not_executed.name: Native source baseline
recommended_experiments_not_executed.design: Use the current PMC XML as the primary source; preserve ordered sections, captions, table bodies, units, figure-reference links and provenance. Group manuscript versions and duplicates before splitting. Use targeted olmOCR only where source text or page-only information is missing.
recommended_experiments_not_executed.reason: Existing XML avoids unnecessary OCR cost; retained structure supports both readable text and later multimodal/entity enrichment.

recommended_experiments_not_executed.name: Filter validation before deletion
recommended_experiments_not_executed.design: Score paragraphs for corruption, topic, section/type and educational value separately. Audit samples with human source checks; retain scores and rejection reasons. Do not use a clinical-utility score to eliminate experimental biology.
recommended_experiments_not_executed.reason: Quality labels measure different properties, and reported clinical/educational filters have task-dependent gains.

recommended_experiments_not_executed.name: Matched training-value ablation
recommended_experiments_not_executed.design: If training is subsequently authorized, compare clean raw article text, scored/selected text, and text with source-linked figure or entity enrichment using the same backbone, token budget, general replay and downstream SFT. Include a no-CPT baseline and report both domain improvements and general retention.
recommended_experiments_not_executed.reason: An OCR/XML agreement score alone cannot show that a corpus improves a foundation model. The current 50-paper batch is an engineering diagnostic, not sufficient evidence for broad training gains.

recommended_experiments_not_executed.name: Protected biological evaluation
recommended_experiments_not_executed.design: Split at paper/version groups before augmentation; protect held-out papers and benchmark items. For sequence tasks add entity/family/species or time-based splits. Measure extraction fidelity against audited sources separately from trained-model performance and synthetic-answer support.
recommended_experiments_not_executed.reason: An XML silver reference, a teacher's quality label, a generated answer and an independent held-out target answer serve different roles.

notes: The original **Dolma** corpus reports **Common Crawl 2,479B; GitHub 411B; Reddit 89B; Semantic Scholar/peS2o 70B; Gutenberg 6B; Wikipedia/Wikibooks 4.3B**, approximately **3,059B total** with its stated tokenizer. This is a reusable dataset's composition, not a biology-only training run or the later Dolma 3 mix. Its academic component can be selected for biology; that selected amount is not given by the 70B headline. [Original Dolma, Table 1 / §8](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.00159)

Dolma is both a **dataset family** and a **curation toolkit**. The original dataset mixes web text, scientific publications, code, books and other authored text, and uses peS2o for its academic component. Reusing a suitable subset is an important acquisition route, not merely a source of general replay. For our research goal, in-domain selection and deduplication against directly acquired papers matter. The toolkit supplies processing machinery; installing it does not acquire the corpus. corpora.corpus: The original **Dolma** corpus reports **Common Crawl 2,479B; GitHub 411B; Reddit 89B; Semantic Scholar/peS2o 70B; Gutenberg 6B; Wikipedia/Wikibooks 4.3B**, approximately **3,059B total** with its stated tokenizer. This is a reusable dataset's composition, not a biology-only training run or the later Dolma 3 mix. Its academic component can be selected for biology; that selected amount is not given by the 70B headline. [Original Dolma, Table 1 / §8](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.00159)

catalog_policy: One record per model family/study/corpus; all dataset budgets, figure and citation policies attach to that record. Preserve source versions, units and unknowns. This is an organization of existing evidence, not a fresh literature census.

migration.import_scope: Public paper/model metadata and links only; no benchmark cases, labels, prompts or raw evaluation outputs copied.
